scope.focus: Textual criticism; Nostra aetate; Fatima original record; liturgical reform and Latin; Humani generis; Mediator Dei
scope.qualification: Each finding is bounded to a specified source claim, not every sentence in its substantive section. No independent theological or French approval.

findings.locator: §§16–19, original languages and copyists' variants
findings.document_finding: Pius XII expressly endorses comparison with inspired originals and textual criticism to recover readings corrupted by copyists.
findings.qualification: This establishes legitimate Catholic methodology, not the motive or author of any particular alleged deletion.

findings.locator: §§20–22, Tridentine Vulgate authenticity
findings.document_finding: Pius XII distinguishes the Latin Vulgate's ecclesial juridical authority from the critical priority of Hebrew and Greek originals.
findings.qualification: This does not remove the defined canon or suggest that each textual witness has equal authority.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §4, Jewish origins and Cross
findings.document_finding: The Council acknowledges Israel's patriarchs, Scriptures and spiritual patrimony while professing Christ's reconciliation by the Cross.
findings.qualification: The paragraph does not state that present rabbinic Judaism and Catholic Christology coincide.

findings.locator: §4, collective guilt and Catholic relations with Jews
findings.document_finding: The document expressly rejects attributing the Passion to all Jews then alive or Jews today, and condemns anti-Semitism.
findings.qualification: An ancient author's polemical manuscript accusation cannot establish collective Jewish culpability.

findings.locator: §4, Abrahamic heritage and evangelical charity
findings.document_finding: The Council explicitly affirms the Jewish root of the Church, calls for study and mutual respect, and retains proclamation of the Cross.
findings.qualification: Respectful dialogue is not an instruction to deny Christ as Messiah.

findings.locator: §3, Catholic description of Islamic faith
findings.document_finding: The Council says Muslims honour Jesus as prophet and Mary but do not acknowledge Jesus as God.
findings.qualification: The Council's esteem for persons and common goods does not imply identical Christian and Muslim Christology.

findings.locator: §§21–23 and 25, council's reform mandate
findings.document_finding: The Council commands a regulated liturgical reform, detailed study and consultation of bishops rather than itself printing the 1969 Missal.
findings.qualification: Subsequent exact textual choices require Paul VI's promulgation and edition comparison.

findings.locator: §22 and §23, authority and organic development
findings.document_finding: The original constitution forbids priests to alter the liturgy privately and requires real ecclesial need and organic development.
findings.qualification: This rule alone cannot prove that an external Protestant observer composed the promulgated Missal.

findings.locator: §23, concrete rule for innovations
findings.document_finding: The Council prohibits innovation absent a genuine and certain ecclesial good and requires organic continuity with earlier forms.
findings.qualification: The norm itself does not resolve every historical judgment about a particular altered prayer.

findings.locator: §§21–23, authority and reform criteria
findings.document_finding: The constitution differentiates lawful competence for alteration from theological and pastoral standards governing its use.
findings.qualification: A rite's juridical promulgation cannot logically establish that every historical criticism lacks substance.

findings.locator: §23, sound tradition and authentic progress
findings.document_finding: The Council requires theological, historical and pastoral inquiry before alteration and growth from inherited forms.
findings.qualification: The requirement neither makes each human liturgical detail immutable nor grants individuals their own authority.

findings.locator: Humani generis §§35–37, origins and spiritual soul
findings.document_finding: Pius XII permits scholarly discussion of evolution of the human body while reserving immediate creation of the rational soul.
findings.qualification: He does not extend that freedom unchanged to the specified polygenist theories.

findings.locator: §37, formulation of polygenism and original sin
findings.document_finding: Pius XII explicitly says Catholics cannot embrace the forms of polygenism he describes due to their unresolved relation to Adam's sin.
findings.qualification: An evolutionary hypothesis and a claim about transmission of original sin are not the same proposition.

findings.locator: §§36–38, scholarly freedom and revelation
findings.document_finding: Pius XII subjects biological-origin hypotheses to scientific and theological scrutiny while maintaining divine creation of souls.
findings.qualification: Science cannot independently determine a revealed supernatural doctrine by genetic evidence alone.

findings.locator: CDF 2000 Message of Fatima, introduction and theological commentary
findings.document_finding: The published text ties the apparition's message to conversion and penance rather than a new completion of the Gospel.
findings.qualification: It does not make all disputed secondary predictions part of the deposit of faith.

findings.locator: 2000 document, manuscript and custody chronology
findings.document_finding: The CDF supplies a dated manuscript, a custody account and Sister Lucia's report identifying her own writing on 27 April 2000.
findings.qualification: Documentation for one manuscript is not affirmative proof of an additional authenticated one.

findings.locator: Ratzinger's theological commentary on public and private revelation
findings.document_finding: Cardinal Ratzinger says public Revelation is complete in Christ and distinguishes private visionary signs from dogmatic revelation.
findings.qualification: The vision's spiritual significance does not authorize replacing Church dogma with a hypothetical unpublished text.

findings.locator: §§21–23, 36 and 116, reform, Latin and chant
findings.document_finding: The constitution calls for organic reform, explicitly preserves Latin and gives Gregorian chant pride of place.
findings.qualification: It did not promulgate the later Roman Missal or categorically prohibit vernacular worship.

findings.locator: §§22–23, competent promulgation and prior study
findings.document_finding: The Council names competent ecclesiastical legislators and demands theological, historical and pastoral investigation of changes.
findings.qualification: No conclusion about the validity of a particular later rite follows merely from the conciliar mandate.

findings.locator: §§23, 36 and 116, organic growth and language continuity
findings.document_finding: The conciliar text supports meaningful continuity, preservation of Latin and Gregorian chant despite allowing measured vernacular expansion.
findings.qualification: A defence of traditional Latin worship is not thereby a rejection of the Council's entire text.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§48–50, liturgy as witness to Catholic faith
findings.document_finding: Pius XII treats the liturgy as testimony to doctrinal faith under magisterial authority and distinguishes mutable ritual forms.
findings.qualification: The encyclical cannot alone settle any specific redactional comparison between old and new Offertory prayers.

findings.locator: §§48–50 and 63–65, doctrinal witness and authorized revision
findings.document_finding: The liturgy's testimony to doctrine and the distinction between divinely instituted and mutable parts are expressly articulated.
findings.qualification: The text precedes and does not authorize or criticize every individual revision of the 1969 Missal.

findings.locator: §§48–50, faith and prayer; §66 Eucharistic worship
findings.document_finding: Pius XII treats liturgical prayer as a doctrinal witness and the Eucharistic sacrificial worship as central to Christianity.
findings.qualification: The legitimate criticism of text choices is not an automatic declaration of sacramental invalidity.

findings.locator: §35 and §51, readings and rich table of Scripture
findings.document_finding: The Council calls for a wider, more varied liturgical provision of Bible readings to the faithful.
findings.qualification: The conciliar requirement alone does not give numeric verse coverage for either lectionary.

findings.locator: §§24, 35 and 51, Scripture in liturgical prayer
findings.document_finding: The Council asks for increased readings and renewed love for Scripture within the liturgical year.
findings.qualification: It does not establish whether later choices omitted specific difficult passages without separate pericope comparison.

findings.locator: §§24 and 51, scriptural inheritance and liturgical reading
findings.document_finding: Scripture is described as constitutive of Christian prayers, rites, and a wider cycle of readings.
findings.qualification: This does not render a historic one-year cycle spiritually useless by definition.

findings.locator: §36, preservation of Latin; §116, Gregorian chant
findings.document_finding: Vatican II says the Latin language is to be preserved and Gregorian chant holds pride of place in the Roman liturgy.
findings.qualification: The same text authorizes vernacular use under defined procedures; it does not legislate Latin-only worship.

findings.locator: §§14, 19, 30 and 36, participation and language
findings.document_finding: The constitution calls for interior and exterior participation, including reverent silence, and permits vernacular expansion.
findings.qualification: It does not reduce participation to comprehension of every word or forbid silence.

findings.locator: §§36 and 116, liturgical language and chant
findings.document_finding: The original council constitution explicitly commits Roman-rite practice to preserving Latin and privileging Gregorian chant.
findings.qualification: Translations and vernacular catechesis can coexist with those commitments.

findings.locator: §§21–23, extent of council's liturgical directions
findings.document_finding: The detailed general norms regulate reform and competent authority, without issuing a universal rule requiring versus populum.
findings.qualification: A negative statement about the Council does not decide the requirements of later rubrics or local directives.

findings.locator: Sacrosanctum Concilium §§22–23, competence and organic development
findings.document_finding: The Council says liturgical legislation belongs to church authority and changes require careful historical and theological examination.
findings.qualification: It does not issue a universal obligation that Eucharistic celebration be directed toward the congregation.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§66–70, the Eucharist as centre of Christian worship
findings.document_finding: The encyclical treats the Eucharistic sacrifice and sacrament as the culminating focus of the Church's worship.
findings.qualification: It does not determine the current lawful Communion distribution method in each jurisdiction.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§58–61, inherited rites, change and authority
findings.document_finding: Pius XII recognizes received ritual forms and holds that only competent authority may alter public rites.
findings.qualification: Respect for an old custom does not independently establish that it remains obligatory in the 1983 Code.

findings.locator: Sacrosanctum Concilium §§21–23, legislative scope and continuity
findings.document_finding: The conciliar constitution states its own doctrinal discipline of liturgical reform, including unchangeable and changeable parts.
findings.qualification: A continuity claim cannot be established by comparing labels while omitting the actual propositions or legal scope.

findings.locator: Sacrosanctum Concilium §22, competences for liturgical regulation
findings.document_finding: The Council explicitly reserves regulation to the Holy See, bishops and other lawful territorial bodies.
findings.qualification: A recognized competence to legislate does not make every prudential decision impeccable or irrevocable.

findings.locator: §§21–23, lawmaking competence distinguished from reform standards
findings.document_finding: The Council's authority and historical-study requirements are distinct parts of a lawful reform assessment.
findings.qualification: Disliking a restriction cannot prove the pope lacks jurisdiction to change disciplinary law.

findings.locator: §23, the need for sound tradition and demonstrated benefit
findings.document_finding: The conciliar rule demands retention of sound tradition and genuine pastoral need before changing rites.
findings.qualification: The rule may justify respectful petitions and critical analysis, not unilateral alteration by priests.

findings.locator: §22, Church authority over worship
findings.document_finding: The original text places governing competence in the Apostolic See and bishops, and prohibits self-authorized change.
findings.qualification: The existence of papal authority does not turn each liturgical preference into dogma.

findings.locator: §22(3), prohibition of individual liturgical improvisation
findings.document_finding: The Council forbids even priests from inserting or removing rites solely on private authority.
findings.qualification: A claim of breach requires identification of the binding missal, rite, date and competent permissions.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§58–59, public worship and unauthorized innovations
findings.document_finding: Pius XII rebukes unauthorized personal innovations and confirms that religious worship is regulated by Church authority.
findings.qualification: A locally approved discipline may be lawful even when a traditionalist dislikes its appearance.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §4, Jewish roots and Christian fulfillment
findings.document_finding: The declaration recalls the Church's grafting into Israel's patrimony and professes Christ as reconciliation by his Cross.
findings.qualification: It does not identify the theology of all later Jewish groups with apostolic Christianity.

findings.locator: §4, Paul and continuing regard for Israel
findings.document_finding: The Council echoes Paul's teaching on gifts and calling and rejects declarations that Jewish people are rejected or cursed.
findings.qualification: This treatment concerns persons and sacred history, not a certification of every current rabbinic proposition.

findings.locator: §4, Old Testament patrimony and all-embracing Cross
findings.document_finding: The text combines esteem for Israel and its scriptural heritage with proclamation of Christ's redemptive Cross.
findings.qualification: The apostolic duty to witness to Jesus is not cancelled by interreligious respect.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §2, acknowledging truth while confessing Christ
findings.document_finding: The document praises elements of truth in other religions and immediately insists the Church must proclaim Christ the way, truth and life.
findings.qualification: It does not state that contradictory religious revelation claims all have the same objective truth.

findings.locator: Humani generis §§1–4, contemporary doctrinal dangers
findings.document_finding: Pius XII describes theological confusions in Church life before Vatican II and calls for sober safeguarding of doctrine.
findings.qualification: This proves preconciliar controversies existed, not that all subsequent conciliar reforms were warranted.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§58–64, prior disputes over Latin and liturgical archaeology
findings.document_finding: Pius XII documents unauthorized vernacular practice and excessive antiquarian reform proposals well before 1962.
findings.qualification: Evidence of preconciliar abuses does not by itself vindicate a later reformer's specific alternative.

findings.locator: §§58–65, received rites and authentic correction
findings.document_finding: Pius XII defends lawful renewal against both private innovations and an uncritical return to antiquity.
findings.qualification: The text is not an endorsement of either total immobility or permanent novelty.

findings.locator: Humani generis §§1–5, 15–20, errors about dogmatic formulation
findings.document_finding: Pius XII criticizes proposals that relativize defined dogmatic terms and theological continuity.
findings.qualification: The encyclical does not assert every ressourcement scholar taught the particular errors under correction.

findings.locator: Humani generis, precautions about the deposit of faith
findings.document_finding: Pius XII rebukes ideas that would convert doctrinal definitions into replaceable approximations.
findings.qualification: Returning to the Fathers need not logically entail repudiating Trent or scholastic developments.

findings.locator: Humani generis §§20–21, doctrinal language and transmission
findings.document_finding: The encyclical insists on continuity and the faithful meaning of ecclesiastically defined doctrine.
findings.qualification: It does not oppose every revision of theological pedagogy or critical textual edition.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§49–59, history and change of liturgy
findings.document_finding: Pius XII documents historical additions and legitimate changes to worship while preserving divine essentials.
findings.qualification: The Liturgical Movement cannot therefore be classified from this text as entirely progressive or entirely antiquarian.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§58–65, permitted development and forbidden antiquarianism
findings.document_finding: The encyclical refuses both unregulated novelty and indiscriminate return to supposedly primitive rites.
findings.qualification: No single liturgical arrangement is proven best for all ages merely because it is old.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§48–50, 58–65, received worship and doctrinal continuity
findings.document_finding: Pius XII places the public worship of the Church under episcopal and papal governance while commending sound liturgical inheritance.
findings.qualification: True internal participation is not reducible to visible activity alone.

findings.locator: Mediator Dei §§49–59, historical reform and varied ceremonial development
findings.document_finding: The encyclical shows that liturgical forms and ceremonies have undergone real historical revisions under lawful authority.
findings.qualification: It does not itself verify the dated 1951 or 1955 Holy Week decree or the merits of those particular changes.

findings.locator: §§58–65, legitimate and illegitimate ways of changing rites
findings.document_finding: Pius XII affirms legitimate liturgical reform and condemns privately revived obsolete usages without authorization.
findings.qualification: The Church's 1955 reforms still require examination in their own officially promulgated texts.

findings.locator: Sacrosanctum Concilium §§21–23, council's doctrinal and pastoral reform framework
findings.document_finding: The constitution provides binding norms for liturgical change without presenting itself as a wholesale replacement of Catholic dogma.
findings.qualification: The actual authority of any separate conciliar proposition still depends on its content and promulgation.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §4, Israel, the New Covenant and collective blame
findings.document_finding: The Council explicitly retains the Church's spiritual relationship with Israel and rejects depicting Jews as accursed by God.
findings.qualification: The paragraph does not teach Christian and contemporary Jewish accounts of Christ are doctrinally identical.

findings.locator: Nostra aetate §4, Christ and Jewish heritage
findings.document_finding: The Council praises shared Old Testament patrimony while explicitly professing Christ's redemptive Cross.
findings.qualification: It condemns anti-Semitism without requiring Christians to suspend apostolic witness.

findings.locator: Memoriale Domini, 1969 consultation and continuing traditional reception
findings.document_finding: The 1969 Roman instruction retained the traditional manner of receiving Communion while permitting limited local exceptions on petition.
findings.qualification: This source addresses the hand/tongue question, not every detail about rail placement or tabernacle architecture.

findings.locator: 1917 Code canon 1262 §2, historical head-covering requirement
findings.document_finding: The 1917 canonical prescription required head coverings for women when entering church and instructed men otherwise.
findings.qualification: That former code was later abrogated; the old prescription is not automatically a present universal canonical obligation.
